column16: club renamed Wexford F.C. in 2017; home kit all pink as Wexford Youths (club page); capacity 2,500 from the season page; source2 (RSSSF) agrees with name and division only, not city, stadium or capacity; founded 6 February 2007; city: Crossabeg, near Wexford town

single 17-club Championship in 2008/09 (row is right); ground and capacity from the season page club table (Riada Stadium, Ballymoney, 5,752, 218 seated), shared with Ballymoney United; colours from the current infobox (red and white stripes, blue shorts), not confirmed for this season; source2: no second publisher page could be read (RSSSF and newspaper pages not reachable); 2008/09 page does not give grounds, ground taken from the 2010/11 page (inference for 2008/09)

relegated to Championship 2 at the end of 2008/09 (row is right); capacity 1,200 (100 seated) from the club page and the 2010/11 season table; source2 (BBC, June 2013) agrees with name, Darragh Park and Castlederg, but dates from 2013, not 2008/09; colours from the current infobox (white with thin black stripes, black shorts)

name change: played 2014 as Galway F.C., renamed Galway United before the 2015 season; founded 2013 as a new club (Galway United claims 1937, inference to use 2013); finished 3rd and won the promotion play-off (row is right); capacity for 2014 unknown (club page gives 4,323 today, 2023 season table 5,000); colours: maroon is the club colour, white second colour is an inference; source2 (Galway Advertiser, Sept 2013) agrees with name and Eamonn Deacy Park; RSSSF ier2014 agrees with name Galway FC and division

first LOI season 2015 (row is right); ground is Stradbrook Road in Blackrock, Dublin, home of Blackrock College RFC, rented; capacity for 2015 unknown (2021 season table gives 1,620); colours from the current infobox (white shirts, green shorts); source2 (the42, March 2015) and balls.ie agree with Stradbrook and First Division; club merged into Bray Wanderers after 2021

first LOI season 2021 (row is right); capacity 5,000 from the 2021 season table, club page gives 4,500 (1,710 seated) today, capacity disagrees; colours from the current infobox (blue with white collar), not confirmed for 2021; source2 (the42, March 2021) agrees with name, Limerick, Markets Field and First Division

first LOI season 2023 (row is right); capacity 1,200 from the club page and the 2023 season table; colours from the current infobox (green with white v-neck), not confirmed for 2023; source2 (Irish Examiner, Feb 2023) agrees with name, Tralee, Mounthawk Park and League of Ireland; RSSSF ier2023 agrees with division
